title: Unify TypeScript SDK emitter for polymorphic shapes with ergonomic discriminators and Zod/JSON-Schema helpers
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Goal: Deliver a single, ergonomic TypeScript emitter that produces both compile-time types and runtime validators for polymorphic/union-shaped structured output. This ticket covers: 1) a compact discriminator tagging pattern that works well for streaming/partial output, 2) generator outputs for Zod and JSON-Schema (for server-side routing and CI checks), 3) runtime guards and progressive-parsing helpers for streaming responses, and 4) example conversion recipes for users migrating from ad-hoc discriminators.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: aligned on problem statement with PM (Lena) and Design (Rui). We need a pattern that: a) surfaces the variant early so streaming parsers can pick a branch, b) minimizes token overhead for high-throughput use-cases, c) is compatible with existing model adapters.

2026-03-03 - Design decision: prefer a short-string discriminator field called '__type' (double-underscore to reduce collision risk) placed as the first emitted key in structured JSON streams. Alternative explored: prefix token markers (-style) but rejected for readability and portability.

2026-03-04 - Engineering note: generator will emit three artifacts per shape: 1) TypeScript type, 2) Zod schema (zod v4), 3) JSON-Schema (draft-07) with discriminator mapping. This mirrors runtime needs: client-side parsing (Zod), server-side routing/validation (JSON-Schema).

2026-03-05 - Trade-offs: we can embed the discriminator as a top-level key (fast parsing) vs an explicit 'kind' wrapper object (safer with namespacing). Chosen top-level '__type' to keep emitted payload shallow; follow-up task to audit collision with user data.

2026-03-06 - Streaming ergonomics: added progressive parser helpers (parseUntilDiscriminator, progressiveZodValidate) to let SDK consumers short-circuit parsing once variant is known. Prototype shows 30-40% latency improvement for 1-token discriminator-emission models.
2026-03-07 - PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ts/pull/981 - contains generator prototype and small end-to-end example. Requesting reviews from @marco, @rachel-security, @lena-pm.

2026-03-08 - Review feedback: Rachel flagged missing KMS/audit implications for JSON-Schema stored fixtures (accepted; added note for secure storage in confluence). Marco requested clearer examples for retry interaction (how to avoid double-applying partial streamed objects on retry).

2026-03-09 - Implementation update: added idempotency guidance and small helper 'applyPartialSafely' to merge progressive object chunks with user-provided dedupe keys. Load tests show no regressions in throughput.

2026-03-10 - Next steps: finalize generator CLI flags, add CI check that validates schema roundtrip (type -> zod -> json-schema -> runtime validator), and expand examples to include a canary in the console sample app.
acceptance_criteria: Generator emits TypeScript types, Zod schemas, and JSON-Schema for all polymorphic shapes in the model manifest
Streaming parser helper can detect '__type' within the first 256 bytes and route to the correct validator without full-string buffering
Examples and migration guide added to SDK README explaining how to move from inline string tags to the new '__type' pattern
CI contains a roundtrip test: generated TS type -> generated Zod -> runtime validation passes for all fixture payloads
Performance: progressive parse path reduces median parse latency by >=20% for streaming responses in internal benchmark
